item.title: Caleb Williams Undergoes X-Ray After Leading Bears to Dramatic Win Over Lions
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Caleb Williams gave the Chicago Bears a Thanksgiving finish they won’t soon forget. After the game, their quarterback underwent an X-ray that briefly gave fans something else to think about. Williams had imaging done following Chicago’s 39-35 comeback victory over the Detroit Lions, according to Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune . The reason for the examination was not disclosed, and there was no immediate indication that Williams would miss time. #Bears QB Caleb Williams just went for an X-ray. He was one of the last players off the field. Was in the locker room for celebration. Could be precautionary. — Brad Biggs (@BradBiggs) November 26, 2026 Williams himself offered a reassuring response after the game, saying he was fine, according to Bleacher Report . He also joined his teammates for the postgame celebration after delivering a performance that moved the Bears into first place in the NFC North. The X-ray is worth watching, particularly after the punishment Williams absorbed against Detroit. For now, though, the available information points to an examination — not a confirmed diagnosis or a change in his availability. Williams delivered when the Bears needed him Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) throws the winning touchdown to Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze (15) during the NFL game against Detroit Lions at Ford Field in Detroit on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26, 2026. The third-year quarterback’s afternoon was far from comfortable. Detroit pressured Williams throughout the game and sacked him four times, including a strip-sack late in the first half that contributed to a safety. He kept coming back. Williams completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Both scoring passes went to Rome Odunze in the fourth quarter, when Chicago needed them most. Trailing 35-24 with approximately eight minutes remaining, the Bears cut into the deficit on a 41-yard connection between Williams and Odunze. Williams then ran in the two-point conversion to bring Chicago within three. The defense gave him another chance when linebacker T.J. Edwards stopped Jahmyr Gibbs short of the marker on fourth down. Williams took over at Chicago’s 32-yard line with 2:17 remaining and moved the Bears toward the end zone. He also converted a fourth-and-1 with his legs to keep the drive alive. With three seconds left, Williams found Odunze in the back right corner of the end zone for a six-yard touchdown, completing a comeback that gave Chicago its only lead of the game. item.title: Michigan basketball gets hammered in Las Vegas as Miami cruises
item.description: Michigan basketball 's skid has continued an blowout fashion. The Wolverines have now lost three consecutive games after falling 97-70 to Miami on Thursday, Nov. 26, in the Players Era Championship tournament at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. Mike Boynton's team gave up more than 50 points in the opening half for the second time in as many games, fell behind by 10 early in the second half and didn't get closer than that the rest of the way. U-M (3-4) once again got lit up from long range, as Jai Lucas' group went 9 of 21 on 3s. It didn't help that moments after halftime, Elliot Cadeau committed his third foul 90 feet from the hoop while Moustapha Thiam committed his fourth just more than two minutes into the second half. Miami (6-2), which led by seven at the break, opened the second half on 22-4 run and never looked back. Matters got worse when Roddy Gayle jr. rolled his ankle just less than seven minutes into the half and had to be helped off the court by trainers. J.P. Estrella continues to be U-M's most consistent player, scoring a team-high 21 points. Cadeau and Trey McKenney were both relatively quiet, scoring 15 and 16 points, respectively. But it was the defense that was the main problem, as the Hurricanes shot 56% from the field. Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. item.description: Credit USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins defensive coordinator Sean Duggan is set to wear custom cleats this Sunday to honor his older brother, Ryan. During the team’s matchup against the New York Jets, the gear supports the Down Syndrome Association of Greater Cincinnati. Duggan will join 40 players and eight coaches in the NFL’s annual “My Cause, My Cleats” initiative, according to the Sun Sentinel . The campaign gives every participant a chance to highlight a personal cause that matters to them. Ryan Duggan, who has Down Syndrome, lives in Cincinnati where their parents still reside. Sean describes his brother as a “baller” and notes that Ryan was a manager on his high school football team. The bond between the two remains strong, with Sean saying they usually talk once a week. Ryan works four days weekly at a local bank and simultaneously holds a board seat with the DSAGC. Baseball and basketball are also played by him in the Special Olympics. Sean recalls how Ryan often asks blunt questions about the team’s defense after games, showing his deep interest in the sport. Ryan’s influence extends beyond family circles, as he is known in his community for his positive attitude. item.description: Le Bris plays down concerns after Sunderland draw at home to Jagiellonia Bialystok Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris insists he is not concerned after his side were held to a 1-1 draw by Jagiellonia Bialystok. Le Bris believes the result is simply part of the process as Sunderland continue to adapt to playing in Europe and the impact of regular squad rotation. “I think it’s part of the journey, you have ups and downs,” he said. “We are building something stronger. It’s really clear when you change the squad, the references between the players are different. “I always need time to adjust different behaviours, so I’m not worried.” The Sunderland boss stressed the importance of continuing to develop despite difficult moments. “Just a part of the journey,” he added. “Sometimes it’s a bit harder and you have to go forward.”

item.title: Rob Gronkowski says Tom Brady ‘told’ him about Aaron Rodgers-esque dispute with former coach
item.description: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images for The Match The Aaron Rodgers debacle has divided people across the nation, with some feeling the veteran quarterback was completely out of line with his comments on Mike McCarthy. Rodgers has now cleared waivers, with the 42-year-old becoming a free agent. Whether a team is willing to take a chance on the controversial QB is another matter. The situation he finds himself in has reminded Rob Gronkowski of some of the situations Tom Brady found himself in. Although Brady and Bill Belichick won a lot of Super Bowls together, there were a lot of rumours around a frosty relationship between the pair. Gronkowski did not name names, but he did provide insight into some of Brady’s private disputes with former coaches. Rob Gronkowski shares how Aaron Rodgers saga reminds him of Tom Brady disputes Brady won an awful lot more than Rodgers over the span of his career, with the former New England Patriots quarterback seemingly ruffling feathers behind the scenes with some of his former coaches. “Being Thanksgiving, this reminds me of the situations that I was in as a player. Aaron Rodgers and Tom Brady are the same level of quarterback: they’re top-tier quarterbacks in this NFL, both Hall of Famers. I’ve seen situations personally with my own eyes where Tom and coaches had disagreements,” Gronk said on Fox Sports. “There’s one thing that Tom did differently: he would dissect it all, hold it in, and still do what’s best for the team, for his teammates, and for the organisation. The disagreements were lethal sometimes. How do I know? Because he trusted in me, and he told me some of them that I would never share with anyone (maybe you guys personally on the low, but no one else in the world). I would see him go out and still be the best player he could be in practice and in games to help win games and win Super Bowls.” The Fox Sports studio did not take well to Rodgers’ comments on McCarthy. There was a clear feeling that the quarterback was only acting with his own interests at heart. Some will agree with this, with some feeling that he has spoken out on behalf of players who are unable to. However, the reaction of the teams around the league will be seen over the coming days and weeks, as Rodgers sits at home as a free agent. Clearly, there will be plenty of concern about the unnecessary distraction signing Rodgers could provide a team at this stage of the season. Coming off of a demoralizing loss to Creighton , Michigan needed to bounce back against Miami (ranked 29th in KenPom) to avoid a three-game skid. Miami was picked to finish fourth in the ACC , and the Hurricanes are tough to score on in the interior, ranking fourth in the country in opponent’s two-point percentage (38.5) and fourth in opponent’s offensive rebounding percentage (22.7). Forward Shelton Henderson leads Miami in scoring (14.3 points per game), and the Hurricanes have several notable transfers, including Acaden Lewis (Villanova), Malik Reneau (Indiana) and L.J. The Hurricanes re-asserted dominance at the start of the second half, jumping out to a 15-point lead that ballooned into a 25-point lead in a hurry. This was a weird environment for a game, with the two teams playing in the middle of Thanksgiving Day in a gym that was mayyyybe 20 percent full based on how it looked on TV. So it’s a bad setting to mount a comeback, but that’s not an excuse; this was the second game in a row that the Wolverines straight up gave up. item.title: Raiders’ special teams can ill afford adding to the team’s overall woes
item.description: (Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images Considering the team’s defense ranks dead last in points allowed and yielding the second-worst amount of yards allowed, the Las Vegas Raiders special teams can ill affording adding to the overall woes. Field position comes at a premium in the NFL and for the Silver & Black, a disadvantage of that nature puts Rob Leonard’s defense in dire straits. Which makes the pair of times Raiders punter AJ Cole III’s boots were blocked by the Denver Broncos in the Week 11 38-24 loss a cause for concern. “I have to watch the tape,” Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak said when asked about the punt protection in the postgame press conference. “Two punts were huge. They were big,” Denver head coach Sean Payton said after the game. “One of them I know was a rush. When you look at what that does field position-wise and just say it’s a 40-yard swing, it’s almost like a turnover.” Even a day later, when the NFL statisticians officially marked the two punts as deflected and not blocked — due to the ball crossing the line of scrimmage — a sour taste remains in the Raiders special teams room. The first deflection occurred in the opening quarter when Denver’s Sai’Vion Jones bull rushed up the middle and changed the trajectory of Cole’s boot with his forearm. The ball eventually settled two yards past the line of scrimmage. The second occurred a quarter later with Dondrea Tillman tipping Cole’s punt limiting the boot to just 27 yards. It was indeed a forgettable Mile High outing for not only Cole, but special teams coordinator Joe DeCamillis. item.description: IMAGO / Icon Sportswire ©Credit - Imago Kevin Durant, like many NFL fans, wasn’t very happy with how the Pittsburgh Steelers released veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers on November 25, a day before Thanksgiving. Initial reports suggested that Rodgers had a falling out with head coach Mike McCarthy. The QB later went on to criticize McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show , and the Steelers released him hours later. Later, rumors about McCarthy having an assistant for a very specific task surfaced. “Happy Thanksgiving, hiring a ice cream sandwich assistant for the day, great idea Mike,” Durant wrote in an X post he uploaded Thanksgiving Day. Durant also showed his support for Rodgers in a separate post by naming him as one of the four NFL players he’d like to have at his table on the holiday. The most shocking claims came from Rodgers himself. Rodgers was benched in favor of Mason Rudolph. The reasons remained unknown until Rodgers himself appeared on The Pat McAfee Show and listed them one by one. Bournemouth were a goal down and a player short after Bafode Diaktie’s first-half sending off but fought back after the break to secure an impressive victory thanks to goals from Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan, with Rose delighted by the character shown by his side. “What a team, what a spirit, what an energy,” he said. “I’m really proud after being one player less, 1-0 down.” Rose also praised the way his players adapted tactically, singling out David Brooks for his performance in an unfamiliar defensive role. “I said to Ty [Adams], sometimes it’s not about tactics and formations and stuff like this,” he said. “Brooksy did a great job when we got one player less, he played just right defender like he played it for 10 years. “We changed in the right moment, everyone did his job on a really high level.” Rose felt Bournemouth’s equaliser after half-time shifted the momentum of the contest and praised his side for continuing to push for the winner. “We created the momentum after the half-time with the first goal and we were just relentless,” he said. “We never stopped to believe in this win and that’s why big, big, big congratulations to the team.”

item.title: Instant analysis from Bears' impressive comeback win vs. Lions
item.description: The Detroit Lions are one of two NFL teams guaranteed to host a game on Thanksgiving. With the Chicago Bears playing in the same division, they get the honor of being the road team a fair amount of times. It usually is them whenever they have a halfway decent chance of being a good team. Chicago helps TV ratings in these spots, especially if the Bears are playoff-bound. This was much more than a holiday match, however, as control of the NFC North was on the line. The Bears and Lions, both 8-2 coming in, were one game ahead of the Minnesota Vikings. We already know the result of the Green Bay Packers’ matchup, as they lost to the Los Angeles Rams on Thanksgiving Eve. Whoever would win this game in Detroit would be 9-2 and have a one-game lead and the early tiebreaker over the other. Having the potential to be the No. 1 seed is one thing, but it’s another to lock in playing at home once the playoffs begin. This game was never going to be easy for Chicago. The Bears haven’t trailed since Caleb Williams came back from injury. That changed when the Lions went up 3-0 early. From there, they mostly led for the rest of the game. The Lions are different than every other team that Chicago played during that winning streak. This is a difficult team to play against closely, let alone win. When the Bears were down and out late in the fourth quarter, it would have been easy to allow the Lions to walk away with a victory. That would have been the result last time they played on Thanksgiving under the previous coaching staff, but things are different now. In a two-minute drill, Caleb Williams drove the team into field goal range looking to tie the game. However, they ended up scoring a touchdown with three seconds left. They took the lead and shut the door on a rugby-style play that the Lions tried to run with no time left. This is one of the most incredible wins of the Ben Johnson era. He finally earned a big win over his old team, and it came in a first-place game in comeback fashion. Williams led the offense in a way that only the most elite can at the end of a win under that type of pressure. The defense had a low-end performance, considering how they've played since Jeffery Simmons arrived, but the offense bailed them out this time. Jared Goff runs one of the best offenses in the NFL, which can be hard for anyone to stop; that doesn't give the Bears an excuse, but it explains a lot. Jahmyr Gibbs ran all over the field against the Bears, but the Bears didn't let it control the outcome of the game. No matter what, there has been one part of the team that steps up whenever they need it most this season. They certainly have the makings of a Super Bowl contender. Now, they have their Thanksgiving win. We wait to see if they can collect wins on Christmas and Valentines Day. item.title: RB Leipzig's Salzburg Pipeline Has Dried Up And Borussia Dortmund Are Reaping The Rewards
item.description: RB Leipzig once had something every Bundesliga club wanted: a direct route to some of Europe's most promising young footballers. Dayot Upamecano, Naby Keïta, Dominik Szoboszlai and Benjamin Šeško all arrived from Red Bull Salzburg. Leipzig could identify talent early, develop it in the Bundesliga and eventually command enormous transfer fees. Now that advantage has disappeared, and Borussia Dortmund are benefiting. According to RB Live , since Šeško and Nicolas Seiwald joined Leipzig in 2023, not a single player has made the same move from Salzburg. Dortmund, meanwhile, has added Joane Gadou to a list that already includes Erling Haaland and Karim Adeyemi. And Gadou is particularly frustrating because the Red Bulls knew exactly who he was. Leipzig Identified Gadou But Dortmund Got Him Dortmund paid €19.5 million for the French centre-back last summer. Already, the 19-year-old is showing why several European clubs wanted him. Against Arsenal on Tuesday, Gadou carried the ball out of defence with remarkable speed before delivering the pass for Maximilian Beier's equaliser. Beier called him an "animal", while sporting director Lars Ricken described the assist as sensational. Standing 1.95 metres tall and capable of reaching 36.55 km/h, Gadou possesses almost everything Leipzig traditionally look for in a central defender. He is physically imposing, exceptionally quick and comfortable advancing with the ball. Leipzig were reportedly interested as early as March 2024, when Gadou was still at Paris Saint-Germain. His name resurfaced on their shortlist earlier this year, but Dortmund won the race. That is what makes this transfer particularly difficult to dismiss. Gadou was not an unknown talent Leipzig overlooked. He was precisely the kind of player their recruitment model was designed to secure. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
